plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero to eliminate all leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the single name mandate.
Add to QQQI, increasing its allocation to 25% to favor income and broad index exposure.

conservative.read: This conservative plan targets around 1.5% per month, focusing on capital preservation. It significantly reduces risk by eliminating leveraged ETFs and diversifying holdings. Expect lower volatility but also more modest growth potential.

plan: Trim SOXL to 3% and SPAL to 1% to reduce leveraged ETF exposure while maintaining a small allocation.
Trim SPY to 25% to reduce concentration and meet the single name mandate.
Buy NET, allocating 4% of the book to add quality tech exposure.
Add AMZU, allocating 4% of the book to further diversify into quality tech.
This plan balances risk and growth, aiming for a diversified portfolio.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets around 2.5% per month, prioritizing risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while blending broad index and quality tech. Expect moderate volatility and growth potential.

plan: Trim SPY to 25% to meet the single name mandate while maintaining significant broad index exposure.
Add to SOXL, increasing its allocation to 6% to lean into leveraged semiconductor exposure.
Add to SPAL, increasing its allocation to 6% to lean into leveraged space exposure.
Add NET, allocating 6% of the book to concentrate in a high-scoring scanner setup.
Add AMZU, allocating 6% of the book to concentrate in another high-scoring scanner setup.
This plan aims for stretched growth by using leverage and concentration.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets around 4% per month, aiming for stretched growth. It significantly increases exposure to leveraged ETFs and concentrates in high-scoring setups. Be aware this raises both upside and drawdown potential, and leveraged ETFs experience daily decay.

plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero to eliminate all high-beta and leveraged exposure.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the single name mandate.
Add to QQQI, increasing its allocation to 30% to rotate into income-focused ETFs.
Add to QQQ, increasing its allocation to 25% for broad index exposure and stability.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly distributions and low drawdown.
income.read: This income plan targets around 1% per month, focusing on parking cash for yield. It rotates into income and broad index ETFs, cutting high-beta names. Distributions are variable, and NAV can still fall in a selloff; this is not a savings account.
